import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Aggregate data for visualization
sales_over_time = coffee_sales.groupby(coffee_sales['date'].dt.to_period('M')).agg({'total': 'sum'}).reset_index()
sales_over_time['date'] = sales_over_time['date'].dt.to_timestamp()

# Create a line plot for total sales over time
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.lineplot(data=sales_over_time, x='date', y='total', marker='o', color='b')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Total Coffee Sales Over Time', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Date', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(True)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Aggregate data for visualization
sales_over_time = coffee_sales.groupby(coffee_sales['date'].dt.to_period('M')).agg({'total': 'sum'}).reset_index()
sales_over_time['date'] = sales_over_time['date'].dt.to_timestamp()

# Create a line plot for total sales over time
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.lineplot(data=sales_over_time, x='date', y='total', marker='o', color='b')

# Add labels and title
plt.title('Total Coffee Sales Over Time', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Date', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(True)

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
